paper: APPSC Group-I Services Prelims (Screening Test) 2019, Notification No. 27/2018, Paper-I General Studies (GS/1G/100, Series A), held 26-05-2019

questions.s: Vijnanesvara wrote Mitakshara at the court of the Chalukya emperor Vikramaditya VI. It was
o: A commentary on the law book of Yajnavalkya
questions.x: Mitakshara, written by Vijnanesvara at the court of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI, is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti. It later became the basis of Hindu inheritance law in most of India.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
(Traveller) — (Reigning Ruler)
questions.x: I-Tsing (Yijing) visited India in the late 7th century CE, nearly a thousand years after Ashoka, so that pair is wrong. The other three travellers did visit during the reigns shown.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following pairs of temples and places is not correctly matched ?
(Temple) — (Place)
questions.x: The Virupaksha temple is at Hampi in Karnataka (another is at Pattadakal), not Thiruvananthapuram. The other three pairs are correct.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Identify the Sultan of Delhi who prohibited drinking of alcohol, introduced market control policy and inflicted severe punishment to rapists.
questions.x: Alauddin Khalji banned liquor, fixed prices through his market control regulations and enforced harsh punishments to keep order.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Point out from the following sufis, who is from the Chishti Sufi Silsilah ?
questions.x: Khwaja Bandanawaz Gesudaraz of Gulbarga was a Chishti saint. Bahauddin Zakariya and Sadruddin Arif were Suhrawardis, and Nuruddin Rishi founded the Rishi order of Kashmir.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The First Round Table Conference was held at London in 1930 to discuss
o: Trial of the Indian National Army prisoners
questions.x: The First Round Table Conference (1930) met to discuss the future constitution of India in light of the Simon Commission report, and dominion status was part of that debate. The final key accepts both option 1 and option 2.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Muhammad Ghori's forces won the battle fought against Prithviraj Chauhan primarily because of
o: The better war slogans of the Turks
Superior war technology of the Turks
questions.x: In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192) Ghori's Turkish army won through superior military organisation and tactics, especially fast mounted archers. Gunpowder came to north India only later, with Babur.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Third Battle of Panipat was fought between
o: Maharaja Ranjit Singh and Madho Rao Scindia
Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas
questions.x: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali of Afghanistan and the Marathas. Akbar defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).
questions.subject: History

questions.s: In January 1565, the Battle of Talikota was fought between
o: The Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccani Sultanates
questions.x: At Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) in 1565 the combined Deccan Sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara army under Rama Raya. Vijayanagara declined after this defeat.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Name the Rana of Mewar who employed Baksariya Muslims in his army :
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: In medieval Deccan, Deshmukh was a village official, who was responsible to
o: Collect land revenue from the peasants and to deposit it in the State treasury
Collect chauth from the local chiefs
questions.x: The Deshmukh was a hereditary revenue officer in the Deccan. He collected land revenue from the peasants and passed it to the state treasury.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: In which year was the Rail network started from Bombay to Thane ?
questions.x: India's first passenger train ran from Bori Bunder (Bombay) to Thane on 16 April 1853.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Chronologically arrange the following Governor-Generals of India.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
(i) Lord Wellesley
(ii) Lord William Bentinck
(iii) Warren Hastings
(iv) Lord Cornwallis
Code :
questions.x: Warren Hastings (1773-85) came first, then Cornwallis (1786-93), Wellesley (1798-1805) and William Bentinck (1828-35).
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Arrange the following rulers of Gupta dynasty in chronological order :
(i) Chandragupta II
(ii) Skandagupta
(iii) Samudragupta
(iv) Kumaragupta I
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
questions.x: The Gupta succession was Samudragupta, then Chandragupta II, then Kumaragupta I, then Skandagupta.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The poet Bana was patronized by which of the following rulers ?
questions.x: Banabhatta was the court poet of Harshavardhana. He wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: When did Portuguese admiral Vasco da Gama come to Calicut ?
questions.x: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) in May 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India round the Cape of Good Hope.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
(Event) — (Year)
questions.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms became the Government of India Act of 1919, not 1929. The other three dates are correct.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: When did the French gain control over Pondicherry ?
questions.x: The French founded Pondicherry in 1674 and lost it to the Dutch in 1693. The Treaty of Ryswick (1697) gave it back, and the key takes 1697 as the year they gained control.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital – the two basic coins of the Sultanate period ?
questions.x: Iltutmish standardised Sultanate coinage with the silver tanka and the copper jital.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who propagated pushtimarga, a religion of grace ?
questions.x: Vallabhacharya founded the Pushtimarga ("path of grace"), a Krishna-bhakti tradition that stresses divine grace.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the code given below :
List I (Monument) — List II (Place)
a. Char Minar — I. Delhi
b. Akbar's Tomb — II. Agra
c. Humayun's Tomb — III. Hyderabad
d. Taj Mahal — IV. Sikandara
Codes :
a b c d
questions.x: Char Minar is in Hyderabad (III), Akbar's Tomb in Sikandara (IV), Humayun's Tomb in Delhi (I) and the Taj Mahal in Agra (II).
questions.subject: History

questions.s: After 1857 revolt, Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal ruler of India, was exiled to
questions.x: After the 1857 revolt the British tried Bahadur Shah Zafar and exiled him to Rangoon in Burma, where he died in 1862.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following rulers of Mysore sent ambassadors to France to bring in European technology, and went on to build a navy ?
questions.x: Tipu Sultan sent embassies to France and to other powers to obtain European technicians and help against the British, and he started building a navy.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who said that, "Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the destruction of the caste system" ?
questions.x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar argued that untouchability could end only with the destruction of the caste system itself, a theme of his "Annihilation of Caste".
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who wrote 'Why I am an Atheist', defending total rejection of all religion on grounds of human dignity and rationalist logic ?
questions.x: Bhagat Singh wrote the essay "Why I am an Atheist" in Lahore jail in 1930.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Why was Doddi Komaraiah, a village militant, murdered on 4 July, 1946, in Janagam taluka of Nalgonda ?
o: He was Razakar who fought against the Deshmukh, hence was murdered.
For trying to defend a poor washer-woman's mite of land.
For defending thugs employed by the deshmukh.
For opposing wartime exactions, rationing abuses, excessive rents and Vethi (forced labour).
questions.x: Doddi Komaraiah was killed by the Visnur deshmukh's men while defending the land of Chakali Ailamma, a poor washerwoman. His death set off the Telangana armed struggle.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
In the Indian context, 'Drain of Wealth' means foreign power in India squeezed Indian economy through various means and transferred it to their native country. This 'surplus' capital caused 'industrial revolution' in their country.
Which of the following foreign ruling powers is associated with the above theory of 'Drain of Wealth' ?
questions.x: Dadabhai Naoroji's drain theory describes how British rule transferred India's wealth to Britain, helping fund its industrial growth.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Who from the following were associated with Subhash Chandra Bose's Indian National Army and faced the trial in Delhi in 1945 ?
(a) P.K. Sahgal
(b) G.S. Dhillon
(c) Shah Nawaz Khan
(d) Bhulabhai Desai
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Codes :
questions.x: INA officers Prem Kumar Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Shah Nawaz Khan were tried together at the Red Fort in 1945. Bhulabhai Desai was their defence counsel, not an accused.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Whose book 'Unto this Last' left a deep impact on Mahatma Gandhi and he even translated it into Gujarati ?
questions.x: John Ruskin wrote "Unto This Last". Gandhi paraphrased it in Gujarati as "Sarvodaya".
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
In the early decades of the twentieth century, caste movements began to proliferate in the Indian society.
Which of the following movements are related to caste-consciousness, leading to caste-movements in particular regions ?
(a) Satyashodhak Samaj in Maharashtra
(b) Self-respect agitation in Tamilnadu
(c) Ghadar movement in Punjab
(d) Bijolia movement in Rajasthan
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Codes :
questions.x: Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj and Periyar's Self-Respect Movement were anti-caste movements. The Ghadar movement was a revolutionary anti-colonial movement, and Bijolia was a peasant movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Choose the correct answer relating to the Supreme Court of India :
o: A Supreme Court Judge addresses his resignation to the Chief Justice of India
The Supreme Court does not have the power to review its own judgments
All Civil and Judicial authorities in India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court
The Supreme Court has the autonomy to make rules for the practice and procedure of court
questions.x: Under Article 145 the Supreme Court makes its own rules of practice and procedure, with the President's approval. Judges resign by writing to the President, and Article 137 lets the Court review its own judgments.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: The Objectives specified in the Preamble contain the basic structure of our Constitution. In this regard choose the correct answer :
o: The idea of basic structure is explained in the Constitution passed on 26th Jan 1950.
Basic structure means that which cannot be amended in exercise of the power under Article 368 of the Constitution.
Parliament is the supreme authority on the basic structure of our Constitution.
Courts have no jurisdiction on basic structure of Indian Constitution
questions.x: The basic structure doctrine was laid down by the courts in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), not written into the Constitution. It means the core features that Parliament cannot amend under Article 368.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Estimates Committee related to which reform to ensure the efficiency of the following ?
questions.x: The Estimates Committee is a financial committee of Parliament. It examines the budget estimates and suggests economies and efficiency in spending, so it serves financial control.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Most important components of secularism are mentioned below, except
o: Prohibition against discrimination on ground of religion, caste, etc.
Sentiments of the majority of people towards cow and against its slaughter.
questions.x: Indian secularism protects everyone, including people with no religion, so "not applicable to irreligious persons" is not one of its components. Equality and non-discrimination are core parts of it.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Social justice enables the Courts to uphold legislation, except
o: To provide a decent standard of living to the working people.
To protect the interest of the weaker sections of the society.
To enact unquestionable laws to protect certain people of the society.
questions.x: Courts uphold social-justice laws that reduce inequality, secure a decent standard of living and protect weaker sections. No law is beyond judicial review, so "unquestionable laws" is the exception.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: A person whose freedom of movement has been taken away by imprisonment or detention does not thereby lose his freedom of
questions.x: The courts have held that a prisoner keeps the fundamental rights that are not incompatible with imprisonment, such as freedom of expression (for example, writing and publishing books). Freedom of movement and freedom to practise a profession are necessarily curtailed.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the Habeas Corpus, choose the wrong answer.
o: Habeas Corpus safeguards the liberty not only of the citizens but also of the persons within the territory.
Writ of Habeas Corpus is not to be entertained when a person is committed to judicial custody or public custody by the competent court.
A petition of Habeas Corpus lies against the executive authority, not available against the private individuals.
The Habeas Corpus petition cannot be dismissed on the ground of imperfect pleadings.
questions.x: Habeas corpus can be issued against private individuals who detain someone illegally, not only against public authorities. So the statement that it lies only against the executive is wrong.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the Directive Principle of State Policy, choose the wrong answer.
o: Directive Principles have been held to supplement Fundamental Rights in achieving a Welfare State.
Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights for implementing the Directive Principles.
It shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
Directive Principles do not confer any enforceable Rights and their alleged breach does not invalidate laws.
questions.x: Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights to give effect to Directive Principles, as long as the basic structure is untouched (for example, Article 31C and the Minerva Mills case). So the statement that it cannot is wrong.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the Governor, all following statements are correct, except
o: Governor is not answerable to either House of the State.
Governor is not answerable to either House of the Parliament.
Governor is not answerable to Council of Ministers.
Governor shall quit his office immediately after expiry of his term.
questions.x: Under Article 156(4) a Governor stays in office after the five-year term ends until a successor takes charge. So the statement that he quits immediately is incorrect.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: The orders passed by the Governor of a State (Article 163) of a State fall in four categories. Find out the category which is not subject to Judicial Review.
o: The exercise of executive power in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution by or under the order of the Governor
Orders passed by the Governor on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister
Where the Governor acts without the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers and acts in his own discretion
questions.x: Article 163(2) says the validity of anything the Governor does in his discretion cannot be questioned on the ground that he should or should not have acted in his discretion. That shields discretionary acts from judicial review.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the Union Council of Council of Ministers, choose the wrong answer.
o: A Council of Ministers must always exist to advise the President.
Even after the dissolution of Lok Sabha, Council of Ministers exists to advise the President.
Even after the resignation of the Prime Minister, Council of Ministers exists to advise the President.
During the period of National Emergency, the President acquires discretionary powers, and can take independent decisions.
questions.x: Even during a National Emergency the President must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74. He gets no independent discretion, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: The Preamble may be invoked to determine the ambit of
questions.x: Courts use the Preamble as a guide to interpret the Constitution, including the scope of Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the Article 15 of the Constitution of India, find the wrong answer.
o: Article 15 is limited to citizens only.
Article 15 clause (1) and clause (2) both are limited to discrimination on grounds of religion, place of birth, etc.
Article 15 permits the State to make special provision for women and children.
Article 15 also permits the State to make any special provisions for SC, ST and socially and economically backward classes of citizens.
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following are not the federal features of the Indian Constitution ?
questions.x: A rigid constitution, a bicameral legislature and an independent judiciary are federal features. A Governor appointed by the Centre is usually counted as a unitary, non-federal feature.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: What option does the government exercise and legislators have when they do not like a decision made by the Supreme Court ?
o: Pass a law challenging the decision
Pass a constitutional amendment that circumvents the decision
Both are options, pass a constitutional amendment that circumvents the decision or pass a law challenging the decision
No options are there before the legislators and executives
questions.x: To get round a judgment, the legislature can either amend the Constitution or pass a new law that removes the basis of the decision. Both routes are available.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the disagreement between the two Houses of the State Legislature, which of the following is correct ?
o: The bill ends and becomes dead
To resolve the issue a joint sitting will be called for
The only power of the Council is to interpose some delay in the passage of the bill
Legislative Council is a resolving body like Rajya Sabha
questions.x: There is no joint sitting in a state legislature. Under Article 197 the Legislative Council can only delay an ordinary bill, by up to three months the first time and one month the second, and then the Assembly's will prevails.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Choose the correct answer from the following :
o: A member of an All India Service can be dismissed or removed only by the Union government.
A member of an All India Service can be dismissed or removed only by the State government also if he serving under the State.
In India, State Government employees administer State laws only.
Union Government through its departments administers Union laws.
questions.x: All India Service officers are appointed by the Centre, so only the Union government can dismiss or remove them, even while they serve a State. State officials in fact administer many Union laws too.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the powers of the President, which of the following is correct ?
o: No previous sanction is required or recommendation of the President for introducing any legislation on any matter.
Courts are debarred from invalidating any legislation on the ground that the President's previous sanction was not obtained.
A money bill can be returned for re-consideration.
President does not have the power of disallowance of a bill of the State legislature, which may have been reserved for his consideration by the Governor of the State.
questions.x: Under Article 255 a law is not invalid just because the required prior sanction or recommendation was not obtained, as long as assent was later given. So courts cannot strike it down on that ground.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Match the following :
a. Reprieve — I. Reduce the amount of sentence without changing its character
b. Respite — II. Substitute one form of punishment for other of a lighter character
c. Remission — III. Awarding lesser sentence
d. Commutation — IV. A stay of execution of sentence
Codes :
a b c d
questions.x: A reprieve stays execution of a sentence (IV), and a respite awards a lesser sentence because of special circumstances (III). A remission reduces the amount of a sentence without changing its character (I), and a commutation substitutes a lighter form of punishment (II).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the pardoning powers, choose the correct answer.
o: Under the Indian Constitution, the pardoning power of the President and Governor are one and the same.
For offences made under Concurrent lists, without the State role, President alone has the pardoning power.
The only authority for pardoning a sentence of death is the President.
As regards suspension, remission, the Governor does not have a concurrent jurisdiction with the President.
questions.x: Under Article 72 only the President can pardon a death sentence. A Governor can suspend, remit or commute a death sentence but cannot pardon it.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: A sitting of the Parliament can be terminated by adjournment, prorogation or dissolution. In this regard choose the correct answer.
o: Adjournment terminates sitting as well as session of the House.
All pending notices including introducing bills lapse on prorogation.
Dissolution ends all business including bills and motions before the Lok Sabha.
Adjournment sine die means terminating a sitting for an indefinite period.
questions.x: Adjournment sine die ends a sitting without fixing a day for the next one. An adjournment does not end the session, and prorogation does not make pending bills lapse (only notices other than those for introducing bills lapse).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following Liberties is sought to be secured to the citizens of India in the Preamble ?
o: Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
questions.x: The Preamble secures "LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship" to all citizens.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Recommendations for the 14th Finance Commission are valid from
questions.x: The 14th Finance Commission (chaired by Y.V. Reddy) covered the five financial years 2015-16 to 2019-20, that is, 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2020.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following bodies concerned with Inter-State relations are Constitutional ?
questions.x: The Inter-State Council is provided for in Article 263 of the Constitution. Zonal Councils come from the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and river water tribunals are set up under a law of Parliament.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: M.M. Punchhi Committee was appointed to study Centre-State relations. Regarding Punchhi recommendations all the following statements are correct except
o: Localising the Emergency Provisions under Articles 355 and 356 either to district or part of district.
Deployment of Central forces without State's consent for a short period.
In appointing the Chief Minister, pre-poll alliance should be treated as one political party.
National Integration Commission shall meet once in two years
questions.x: The Punchhi Commission (2010) recommended localising emergency provisions, letting the Centre deploy forces briefly without State consent, and treating a pre-poll alliance as one party when appointing a Chief Minister. The statement about a National Integration Commission meeting every two years is not among its recommendations as framed, so it is the exception.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Regarding the composition of the Legislative Council, all following statements are correct, except
o: 1/3rd of the total number of Council shall be elected from local bodies.
1/12th of the total number of Council shall be elected by graduates.
1/12th of the total number of Council shall be elected by Teachers.
1/13th of the total number of Council shall be elected by Legislative Assembly.
questions.x: Under Article 171 one-third of the members are elected by the Legislative Assembly, not one-thirteenth. One-third come from local bodies, one-twelfth from graduates, one-twelfth from teachers, and about one-sixth are nominated.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: The President may appoint a Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union Territory. Such Governor in the administration of Union Territory shall exercise his functions
o: On the aid and advice of his Council of Ministers.
As such administrator independently of his Council of Ministers.
Governor can form his choice of Council of Ministers for aid and advice.
A Governor of a State cannot be appointed as an Administrator of a Union Territory.
questions.x: Under Article 239(2) a Governor appointed administrator of an adjoining Union Territory acts there independently of his State Council of Ministers.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Parliament has the power to enact laws with respect to a matter in the State list in the national interest. In this regard choose the wrong answer.
o: On the request of two or more States.
Legislation for giving effect to International agreements.
Both Union and State governments have absolute freedom to make laws related to Concurrent list.
Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by the Legislatures of States.
questions.x: On Concurrent List subjects a Union law prevails over a conflicting State law (Article 254), so neither side has absolute freedom. Parliament can legislate on State subjects at the request of States (Article 252) and to implement treaties (Article 253).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Due to the existence of which article, the State cannot interfere and dispossess a person's property except in accordance with the procedure established by law ?
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key. The relevant provision is Article 300A, which is not among the options.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: State Government can pass a law imposing restrictions on goods imported from other States. Such law shall be moved in the Legislature of a State without the previous sanction of the
questions.x: The proviso to Article 304(b) says a bill imposing reasonable restrictions on trade with other States can be introduced in a State legislature only with the President's previous sanction.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: "Sustainable Development is the development that meets the needs of the present without compromising on the ability of future generations to meet their own needs." Who has given this definition ?
o: Research paper by David Pearce, Giles Atkinson in 1993 [Center for Social and Economic Research on Global Environment]
"Beyond Growth : The Economics of Sustainable Development", book written by Herman Daly in 1996
Research paper by John Hartwick in 1977
questions.x: This standard definition comes from "Our Common Future" (1987), the report of the World Commission on Environment and Development chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Out of the options given below, what should be the basic goal of "Sustainable Development" ?
questions.x: The key treats equity, meaning fairness within and between generations, together with inclusive growth as the basic goal of sustainable development.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which is the curve that explains the relationship in between economic growth and environmental degradation ?
questions.x: The Environmental Kuznets Curve is an inverted U: pollution rises with income at first and falls after a certain level of income. The Laffer curve is about tax rates, the Lorenz curve about inequality and the Phillips curve about inflation and unemployment.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: According to 2010 Human Development Index calculated (Compiled and Computed from UNDP Human Development Report) for 169 countries, what is the rank of India ?
questions.x: In the UNDP Human Development Report 2010, India ranked 119th of 169 countries.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the approach followed by National Institution For Transforming India Aayog in the economic policy making ?
questions.x: NITI Aayog replaced the top-down Planning Commission in 2015. It works through cooperative federalism, with the States as equal partners in policy-making.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Though removal of unemployment is mentioned as one of the objectives of economic planning in all Five Year Plans, from which plan onward is serious concern shown for solving the unemployment problem ?
questions.x: The key takes the Fifth Plan (1974-79), with its "Garibi Hatao" focus on poverty and employment, as the point from which unemployment got serious attention.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
o: About 60% of agricultural lands have irrigational facilities.
About 55% of net cropped area is rainfed in India.
HYVP was mainly constrained for 5 crops.
Green revolution led to intensive cultivation.
questions.x: Only about half or less of India's net sown area is irrigated, and more than half is rainfed. So the claim that about 60% has irrigation is incorrect.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: To enhance food security and to make Indian Agriculture more resilent to climate change, which programme was started in 2011-12 ?
questions.x: The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. It aims to make farming more productive and climate-resilient, and the key dates its start to 2011-12.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which sector comprises water supply ?
questions.x: In Indian national accounts, "electricity, gas, water supply and other utility services" is counted in the secondary (industry) sector.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the main objective of 12th Five Year Plan ?
questions.x: The theme of the 12th Five Year Plan (2012-17) was "Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth".
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Among the following National Income Concepts, find out the correct one :
o: Gross Domestic Product at Market Price = Gross National Product – Depreciation
Gross Domestic Product at Market Price = Gross National Product at Market Price – Net Income from Abroad
Gross Domestic Product at Market Price = Gross National Product at Market Price – Net Indirect Taxes
Net Domestic Product at Market Prices = Net Domestic Product – Net Indirect Taxes
questions.x: GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad, so GDP at market price equals GNP at market price minus net income from abroad. Subtracting depreciation gives the net figures, and subtracting net indirect taxes gives factor cost.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the method used to calculate chronic unemployment ?
questions.x: Usual status uses a reference period of a whole year, so it captures long-term or chronic unemployment. Weekly and daily status capture seasonal and partial unemployment.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: According to the NSSO 68th round, what is the rate of unemployment in India based on usual status unemployment method?
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: In India, in which year was the "Special Economic Zone" policy announced ?
questions.x: The SEZ policy was announced in April 2000, and the SEZ Act of 2005 came into force in 2006. The final key accepts both 2000 and 2006.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: According to United Nations' Millennium Development Goals Programme (2011-2012), what is the percentage of population below the poverty line in India ?
questions.x: Using the Tendulkar method, 21.9% of India's population was below the poverty line in 2011-12. This figure was used in India's MDG reporting.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: At present with which name is Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (1999) implemented ?
questions.x: SGSY was restructured in 2011 as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, branded "Aajeevika". The final key gives Aajeevika.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the basic goal of "Mission Indradhanush" launched in 2014 by Central Government ?
o: Providing irrigational facilities to agricultural land holdings
Encouraging entrepreneurs for the establishment of small business units
questions.x: Mission Indradhanush, launched in December 2014, aims at full immunisation of children and pregnant women against vaccine-preventable diseases.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: In relation to Andhra Pradesh, which of the following applications has received CSI Nihilent Best e-governance Award during the year 2017 – 18 ?
questions.x: The final key gives D-Krishi, an Andhra Pradesh agriculture application, as the winner of the CSI-Nihilent e-Governance award for 2017-18.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which organization launched Rupay card ?
questions.x: RuPay, India's domestic card payment network, was launched by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in 2012.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which is the program that has the theme "One Nation – One Scheme" ?
questions.x: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (2016) replaced the earlier crop insurance schemes with a single national scheme under the slogan "One Nation – One Scheme".
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: During which period did India have continuous current account surplus ?
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the maturity period of treasury bills issued by Government of India ?
questions.x: The Government of India currently issues treasury bills of 91, 182 and 364 days.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Basel III implementation in India ?
o: Minimum Tier 1 capital ratio should be 8%
Minimum total capital ratio should be 9%
Minimum total capital ratio plus capital conservation buffer should be 11·5%
questions.x: Under RBI's Basel III norms the minimum Tier 1 ratio is 7%, not 8%. The total capital ratio is 9%, which becomes 11.5% with the 2.5% conservation buffer.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which of the following in general is eligible as a borrower under National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) ?
questions.x: NRLM lends to the poor mainly through women's self-help groups and their federations, which get revolving funds and bank linkage.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the objective of National Credit Fund for Women, launched by Government of India in the year 1993 ?
o: Empowering women by providing micro finance
Making women self-reliant to take part in the decision making process
To meet the asset needs of poor and assetless women in the informal sector
questions.x: The National Credit Fund for Women, later the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, was set up in 1993 to meet the credit needs of poor and assetless women in the informal sector. The key uses that wording.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: According to 2014 Reorganization Act, after the bifurcation of the State how many revenue divisions are there in Andhra Pradesh ?
questions.x: After bifurcation in 2014, residual Andhra Pradesh had 13 districts with 50 revenue divisions, according to the key.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: After bifurcation, according to the suggestions of NITI Aayog who has to take the construction responsibility of Polavaram Project ?
o: Divided between State and Central Governments equally
State Government with the help of Central Government
questions.x: Polavaram was declared a national project under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014. On NITI Aayog's suggestion the State government was made responsible for building it, with the Centre funding it.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Recently announced South Coastal Railway zone comprises of
questions.x: The South Coast Railway zone, announced in February 2019 with headquarters at Visakhapatnam, was to have the Guntakal, Guntur and Vijayawada divisions. The Waltair division was split, with a new Rayagada division going to East Coast Railway.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: What is the name of the project launched with the objective of computerization of Urban, Local bodies ?
questions.x: The final key gives e-Suvidha, the project for computerising urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which district in Andhra Pradesh has the largest area under food crops ?
questions.x: The final key gives West Godavari, a major rice-growing delta district, as the district with the largest area under food crops.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Match the following List I with List II (Northern hemisphere) and choose the correct answer.
List I — List II
a. Winter solstice — I. December, 22
b. Summer solstice — II. June, 21
c. Vernal equinox — III. March, 21
d. Autumnal equinox — IV. September, 23
Codes :
a b c d
questions.x: In the northern hemisphere the winter solstice falls around 22 December and the summer solstice around 21 June. The vernal equinox is around 21 March and the autumnal equinox around 23 September.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The boundary between crust and mantle is ________ discontinuity.
questions.x: The Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity separates the crust from the mantle. The Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle from the core, and the Conrad discontinuity lies within the crust.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The bottom topography of an Ocean can be shown by
questions.x: A hypsometric curve shows how much of the Earth's surface lies at each height above or depth below sea level, so it represents the relief of the ocean floor.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Yellowstone National Park which is famous for geysers/hot springs is located in
questions.x: Yellowstone, the world's first national park (1872), is in the USA, mainly in Wyoming. It is famous for geysers such as Old Faithful.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which one among the following is a Volcanic Mountain ?
questions.x: Mount Etna in Sicily is one of the world's most active volcanoes. Mont Blanc and Everest are fold mountains.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which one of the following lakes is not part of the Great Lakes of North America ?
questions.x: The Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario. Lake Victoria is in East Africa.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following two statements and choose the appropriate answer :
A. Gorges and Canyons represent V- shaped valleys.
B. Gorges are the extended forms of Canyons.
o: Both A and B are correct
Neither A nor B are correct
questions.x: Gorges and canyons are deep, V-shaped river valleys. It is the canyon that is the extended form of a gorge, not the other way round, so B is wrong.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Arrange the following constituents (in terms of their quantity) in the atmosphere in descending order :
questions.x: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.93% argon and 0.04% carbon dioxide.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/s rightly explain/s about tropopause ?
(i) Seasonal variation occurs in the height of tropopause.
(ii) It is the transition zone between troposphere and stratosphere.
(iii) It lies below the stratosphere
questions.x: The tropopause is the transition zone between the troposphere and the stratosphere, so it lies just below the stratosphere. The final key accepts only (ii) and (iii), although its height does in fact vary with season and latitude.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Wind in the northern hemisphere is deflected towards right due to
questions.x: The Coriolis force, caused by the Earth's rotation, deflects moving air to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern hemisphere.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Doldrums extend on both sides of
questions.x: The doldrums are the calm equatorial low-pressure belt, roughly 5°N to 5°S of the Equator.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The Suez Canal connects
questions.x: The Suez Canal in Egypt joins the Mediterranean Sea at Port Said to the Red Sea at Suez.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which of the following is not a warm ocean current ?
questions.x: The Humboldt (Peru) Current is a cold current flowing north along the west coast of South America. The Agulhas, Brazil and Kuroshio currents are warm.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which among the following has the highest albedo ?
questions.x: Fresh snow reflects about 80-90% of incoming sunlight, far more than sand, grass or water.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Zulu tribes are found in
questions.x: The Zulu are a Bantu people of South Africa, mainly in KwaZulu-Natal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List I (Crops) — List II (Chief Producer)
a. Barley — I. Karnataka
b. Groundnut — II. Uttar Pradesh
c. Ragi — III. Gujarat
d. Rice — IV. West Bengal
Codes :
a b c d
questions.x: The leading producers are Uttar Pradesh for barley (II), Gujarat for groundnut (III), Karnataka for ragi (I) and West Bengal for rice (IV).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which one of the following Islamic countries is predominantly of Shia sect ?
questions.x: Iran is the largest Shia-majority country, with around 90% Shia Muslims. Pakistan and Afghanistan are mainly Sunni, and the key gives Iran.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Karaganda basin is famous for
questions.x: The Karaganda basin in Kazakhstan is one of the largest coalfields of the former Soviet Union.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Danube river flows into
questions.x: The Danube rises in Germany's Black Forest and flows east through central and eastern Europe into the Black Sea, through a delta in Romania.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The 'Hottentots' are
o: Negritos of Sri Lanka having brown colour
questions.x: "Hottentots" is an old colonial name for the Khoikhoi, traditionally nomadic herders of south-western Africa.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: There is a place A with longitude 060° West. There is another place B with longitude 090° East. If, local time at place A is 10 a.m, what would be local time at place B ?
questions.x: The longitude difference is 60 + 90 = 150 degrees, which is 150 × 4 minutes = 10 hours. B lies east of A, so it is ahead: 10 a.m. plus 10 hours is 8 p.m.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Identify the pair that is not correctly matched
Satellite Navigation System — Owned by
questions.x: GLONASS is Russia's satellite navigation system, not the United Kingdom's.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
Dam/Lake — River
questions.x: Kolleru Lake is a natural lake lying between the Godavari and Krishna deltas. It is not formed on the Krishna, so that pair is the mismatch.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
El-Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every three to seven years. Consider the following statements in this regard :
A. The appearance of warm currents off the Coast of Peru in the Eastern Pacific.
B. The word El-Nino means 'Christ Child' because the current appears around Christmas in December.
C. El-Nino was one of the reasons for the deficit rainfall in India (2014).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.x: El Nino is the warming of the eastern Pacific off Peru, and its name means "Christ Child" because it appears around Christmas. It contributed to India's deficient 2014 monsoon, so all three statements are correct.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Israel has common border with
questions.x: Israel borders Lebanon to the north, Syria to the north-east, Jordan to the east and Egypt to the south-west.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: A country with a crude birth rate of 44 and a crude death rate of 11 would have an annual rate of natural increase of
questions.x: Natural increase is the birth rate minus the death rate: 44 - 11 = 33 per 1,000 people, which is 3.3% a year.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which of the following groups of countries is arranged in descending order of area ?
questions.x: By total area the largest countries are Russia, then Canada, then the USA, then China. The USA and China are close, and the order depends on how territorial waters are counted.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which is the mountain between the Black Sea and Caspian Sea ?
questions.x: The Caucasus Mountains run between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Sierra Nevada is the name of
questions.x: The Sierra Nevada is a mountain range in the western United States, mainly in California. Mount Whitney is its highest peak.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which of the following is not a coal field ?
questions.x: Mosabani in Jharkhand is known for copper mining. Raniganj, Umaria and Korba are coalfields.
questions.subject: Geography
